sentences.text: Heard Mr. L. R. Mazumder, learned counsel for the petitioners.

Also heard Mr. R. K. Talukdar,
learned Standing Counsel for the NHIDCL representing the respondent Nos. 1, 2 and 5.
Page No.# 3/3 2.
The petitioners claim that their lands were acquired in exercise of power under the National Highways Act, 1956.

It is the grievance of the petitioners that though zirat compensation was Page No.# 1/3 vs The Union Of India And Othrs on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122811626/
2 determined and paid to them but same is much less then what they expected.
Accordingly, they filed an application before the competent authority for re-assessment.

As the award was already passed,
such application was rightly not considered.

3. In terms of Section 3G(5) of the National Highways Act, 1956, the petitioners are left with the remedy to agitate their grievance before the Arbitrator and it is on record that the Arbitrator has already been appointed.

However, instead of approaching the Arbitrator, the petitioners have approached before this court by way of this writ petition which in the considered opinion of this Court, liable to be dismissed inasmuch as there is no requirement of any reference by the competent authority under Section 3G(5) of the National Highways Act, 1956, except in case of dispute as regards apportionment under Section 3H(4) of the National Highways Act, 1956.
4. That being the position, the writ petition stands dismissed.
5. It is needless to say that petitioners shall have always the right to agitate their grievance under Section 3G(5) of the National Highways Act, 1956, as permissible under law.
